claims.statement: Most revised Waste Shipment Regulation provisions and DIWASS went live on 21 May 2026, replacing paper with electronic exchange for relevant cross-border procedures.
The Commission describes DIWASS as the system for electronic submission and exchange of waste-shipment information and documents.

contrary_evidence: DIWASS and national systems may permit direct use or native ERP integration, and large waste operators can build connectors internally.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: country-pair route rules and anonymised authority rejection-resolution patterns
fingerprint.customer: cross-border waste brokers, recovery facilities and specialist carriers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: ERP adapter, dispatch block and exception console sold as site subscription plus shipment usage
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: facility or broker pays per connected site and successfully issued movement packet
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a notified or green-listed waste load is ready to move but its digital records are incomplete or inconsistent

founder_fit: Rules/data integration is compatible with part-time analytical work and low-touch reseller sales. UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESIS: PLN 80000 funds one route and one ERP pilot before expansion.
risks: A dispatch block or incorrect status could cause costly delays.
Interoperability changes across authorities may create heavy support.

structure.control_point: digital movement-document issuance before waste truck dispatch
structure.critical_dependency: DIWASS endpoint credentials and national-authority status responses

thesis: Build an interoperability connector between weighbridge/waste ERP records and DIWASS, preventing a cross-border truck dispatch until notification, consent, carrier and load records agree. A route-and-error corpus compounds into faster exception resolution for brokers operating across several national systems.
title: DIWASS Dispatch Connector for Waste Brokers
uncertainties: Production API access for a small integrator
